title: DMS Setup — Initialization JSON
description: The sole Thronebound Awakening character-creation input. Paste the complete JSON object generated by the separate Dungeon Generator scenario; DMS validates it atomically before creating authoritative Tier 0 state.

keys: Lustria, nexus realm of Lustria, artificial nexus realm
value: Lustria is an artificial nexus realm attributed to the Architect. Dungeon gates connect it to otherwise separate worlds. Its immense, shifting landscapes contain magical ecosystems, contested resources, and ruins older than present civilizations. No current power has proven itself Lustria's original inheritor, and the realm's intended purpose remains unknown.
title: Lore — Nexus Realm of Lustria
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: the Architect, creator of Lustria, Architect mystery, Architect's purpose
value: The Architect is the presumed maker of Lustria, dungeon thrones, and the nexus's interworld design. Current peoples possess evidence of the Architect's work but no confirmed knowledge of the creator's identity, species, motives, location, or ultimate purpose. Apotheosis may reveal capabilities without resolving those mysteries.
title: Lore — The Architect
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Architect ruins, Architect relics, ancient nexus ruins, energized relic material
value: Ruins and artifacts attributed to the Architect predate Lustria's present powers. Their materials, energy, and functions can support research, construction, portal studies, and dungeon development. Similar design does not prove every ruin served the same purpose, and recovered capabilities do not reveal the Architect's identity or intent.
title: Lore — Architect Ruins and Relics
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian peoples, native Lustrians, Lustrian city-states, Lustrian nomads
value: Lustria contains peoples from countless connected worlds and communities that consider themselves native to the nexus. Empires, kingdoms, refugee city-states, nomadic societies, faiths, colonies, and adventurer communities coexist. No ancestry or culture represents every Lustrian, and claims of original inheritance remain disputed.
title: Lore — Lustrian Peoples
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: crossworld culture, connected-world customs, portal diaspora, interworld community
value: Lustrian communities mix languages, customs, religions, technologies, and magical traditions carried through dungeon gates. Some preserve a strong Homeworld identity; others form new portal diasporas or blended cultures. Familiar ancestry does not guarantee shared values, and comparable practices may arise from unrelated worlds.
title: Lore — Crossworld Culture
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dominion of Lustria, Dominion Overseers, Dominion tribute, dungeon regulation
value: The Dominion claims sovereignty over much of Lustria and fields its largest organized military. It presents itself as guardian of nexus stability and regulates dungeons, gates, tribute, and strategic regions. Because defeated dungeons may become dormant and reform, Dominion policy emphasizes surveillance, restriction, political control, and containment rather than relying on permanent eradication.
title: Lore — Dominion of Lustria
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: dungeon throne, throne-core, Architect throne, dormant throne
value: A dungeon throne is an enduring Architect construct that acts as the dungeon's core and heart. It channels Lustrian power and stabilizes dungeon functions. A defeated or masterless dungeon may enter dormancy, rebuild, and reconnect because the throne's underlying principle persists even when its current manifestation is lost.
title: Lore — Dungeon Thrones
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Thronebound bond, bound Dungeon master, throne bond, Dungeon's chosen master
value: The Thronebound is the individual bound to a dungeon throne as its active master and interpretive will. The bond grants System access, Gate Authority, and influence over the dungeon's development while tying the Thronebound's progression to the throne. It does not erase personality, origin, responsibility, or outside relationships.
title: Lore — Thronebound Bond
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Theme, thematic Dungeon, inherited Dungeon Theme, Theme expression
value: A Dungeon Theme is the pattern through which its throne and Thronebound express architecture, rooms, resources, inhabitants, hazards, abilities, and atmosphere. The same mechanical function can manifest in radically different forms. The Thronebound's choices shape interpretation, and an inherited or divine Theme does not dictate morality.
title: Lore — Dungeon Themes
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon growth, throne development, dungeon expansion, Theme development
value: A dungeon grows by increasing the stable power and complexity its throne can support. Tier advancement unlocks new facilities and higher-order functions; construction creates their themed manifestations; Expansion increases a facility's working scale; facility Tier Ups improve its quality and yield. Growth need not correspond to a larger mapped floor plan.
title: Lore — Dungeon Growth
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Gate Authority, personal Dungeon portal, return portal, portal stability
value: Gate Authority is a Thronebound's ability to invoke the dungeon's nexus connection, not necessarily a learned spell. Unless externally suppressed, it can open a limited return portal from the Thronebound's position to the dungeon. Early use is small, brief, and constrained by the dungeon's daily portal stability. Travel outward follows separate Anchor rules.
title: Lore — Gate Authority
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian magic, innate magic, learned magic, Symbology
value: Lustria is highly saturated with mana. Magic includes innate gifts and learned disciplines: bodily enhancement, sensory or mana affinity, Symbology, incantation, spirit work, healing, protection, and destructive arts. Connected worlds may possess their own magic or comparable forces, so Lustrian scholars classify effects without requiring one universal theory.
title: Lore — Lustrian Magic
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: enchanted craft, Lustrian artificing, magical equipment, crafted enchantment
value: Lustrian craft binds magical function into tools, armor, weapons, vehicles, structures, and consumables. Methods include Symbology, alchemy, spirit work, crystal engineering, biological cultivation, and imported technologies. An item's Grade measures refinement; its form and operating theory remain culturally and thematically specific.
title: Lore — Enchanted Craft
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian Evolution, Evolution breakthrough, magical metamorphosis, evolved being
value: Evolution occurs when a being accumulates enough power and stability to contain and express a more advanced state. Results may be subtle, biological, magical, technological, or entirely non-biological. Evolution usually improves capability, resilience, and lifespan, but it does not guarantee visible transformation, immortality, or identical outcomes across species.
title: Lore — Evolution
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian ecosystems, mana-bearing flora, magical fauna, artificial ecology
value: Lustria contains crystalline deserts, bioluminescent forests, mana-bearing plants, metal-skinned beasts, and other ecologies that cross ordinary biological categories. Mana, Resonance Cores, dungeon emissions, ancient systems, and neighboring Sectors can influence an ecosystem. Adjacent environments may differ radically without being illusory.
title: Lore — Lustrian Ecosystems
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian resource Site, resource vein, harvest Site, extractable vein
value: A Lustrian resource Site is a specific vein, grove, deposit, ruin, creature habitat, or magical phenomenon that can yield useful materials. A dungeon must discover and assess a Site before targeting it. Extraction depends on access, ownership, logistics, remaining reserves, danger, and compatible facilities rather than discovery alone.
title: Lore — Lustrian Resource Sites
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian Adventurer Guild, Guild quest, adventurer rank, dungeon raid
value: Adventurer Guilds professionalize dangerous work that would otherwise require armies. They operate in major cities, train and rank members, and connect clients with qualified adventurers. Dominion authorities sponsor many operations, while private and illegal patrons also commission work. Adventurers may protect, exploit, raid, or work for dungeons according to shifting loyalties.
title: Lore — Adventurer Guilds of Lustria
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: rival Dungeon, rival Thronebound, competing Dungeon, Dungeon rivalry
value: Rival dungeons compete for territory, gates, resources, followers, and influence. Their Thronebound range from new claimants to established powers with servants, allies, and political networks. A rival is not automatically hostile; competition may become trade, alliance, espionage, tribute, sabotage, a raid, or war.
title: Lore — Rival Dungeons
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon politics, Dungeon diplomacy, Dungeon alliance, Dungeon tribute
value: Dungeons act as political powers once others can identify and negotiate with them. Relations may involve recognition, secrecy, treaties, trade, alliances, tribute, vassalage, espionage, territorial boundaries, or war. Dungeon Tier affects leverage but does not decide legitimacy, trust, or diplomatic outcome by itself.
title: Lore — Dungeon Politics
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian merchant guild, cross-portal trade, portal merchants, interworld commerce
value: Merchant guilds move goods, information, and contracts among Lustrian factions and through stabilized dungeon gates. Where rare resources or portal access are involved, their leverage can rival local rulers. Trade connects incompatible world economies through barter, Lustrian Marks, contracts, and negotiated access to transportation.
title: Lore — Lustrian Trade
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian native interests, resource stewardship, local resource rights, indigenous resource claim
value: Lustrian resources may already be inhabited, claimed, cultivated, revered, or protected. Local communities often value territorial rights and long-term stewardship even where a dungeon sees an unused resource vein. Ownership and cultural significance must be discovered rather than assumed absent.
title: Lore — Native Resource Interests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon expansion conflict, contested extraction, territorial extraction dispute, expansion resistance
value: Dungeon construction, extraction, and territorial control can disrupt existing communities, ecologies, trade routes, and claims. Conflict may be avoided or intensified through reconnaissance, negotiation, compensation, stewardship, secrecy, coercion, or conquest. Mechanical access to a resource does not establish uncontested ownership.
title: Lore — Dungeon Expansion Conflict
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Tier system, nexus maturity, dungeon throughput, Tier advancement
value: Dungeon Tier is Lustria's conventional measure of a throne-dungeon nexus's maturity and stable throughput. It measures how much power the dungeon can safely draw, stabilize, distribute, and express. Tier does not directly measure physical size, room count, army size, or the Thronebound's personal strength. Each Tier from 0 through 10 has its own classification card.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tiers
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Administrator, Administrator manifestation, major-linked individual, Administrator summoning
value: Administrators are sapient major-linked individuals created, summoned, or manifested through a throne's interpretation of Dungeon Theme, active roles, current needs, Thronebound influence, and accumulated knowledge. Their existence and growth strongly benefit from the dungeon, encouraging loyalty without removing personality, disagreement, ambition, or independent relationships.
title: Lore — Dungeon Administrators
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon-supported population, Worker origin, Soldier origin, population manifestation
value: A dungeon creates or acquires Workers and Soldiers through Theme-consistent means such as summoning, fabrication, growth, animation, spirit embodiment, recruitment, or immigration. Relevant Administrators stabilize and organize the process but need not be the population's biological source. The method is narrative; the Dungeon System treats each result as supported population.
title: Lore — Dungeon-Supported Population
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian power classification, Dominion appraisal, capability classification, crossworld appraisal
value: Dominion and Guild appraisers use standardized Tier, Class, Grade, Rank, and specialization terms to compare capabilities from incompatible worlds. These labels describe measurable function without dictating appearance or metaphysics. Evolution Tier, Class, Class Tier, Skill, Trait, Rank, and Grade each have separate meanings and individual cards.
title: Lore — Lustrian Power Classification
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon resource roles, Construction resource, Sustenance resource, Development resource
value: Dungeon Systems classify themed substances by strategic role rather than appearance: Construction builds and upgrades; Sustenance supports population; Development advances linked characters; Energy powers dungeon functions and serves as internal currency. Stone, steel, living bone, nanomaterial, condensed shadow, or another substance may fill the same role.
title: Lore — Dungeon Resource Roles
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Construction Resource role, dungeon building material, facility construction material, room upgrade material
value: The Construction Resource is the dungeon's themed material for building facilities, expanding them, and completing structural Tier Ups. Its name, appearance, source, and collection method are unique to the Dungeon Theme. The System tracks its amount and role consistently even when it is metal, crystal, living matter, force, or something stranger.
title: Lore — Construction Resource
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Sustenance Resource role, population sustenance, dungeon food resource, workforce upkeep resource
value: The Sustenance Resource supports the dungeon's Workers, Soldiers, and other dependent population. It may be food, biomass, mana, fuel, maintenance substrate, spiritual essence, or another Theme-consistent necessity. Its narrative form is player-defined; facilities produce and consume it through the shared dungeon economy.
title: Lore — Sustenance Resource
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Development Resource role, linked character development, Administrator development material, Thronebound advancement material
value: The Development Resource is the themed substance used to advance the Thronebound and Administrators. It supports Class Ups, training, Rank development, and other linked-character functions when appropriate facilities are available. It is distinct from general Energy even if the Dungeon Theme describes both as related forces.
title: Lore — Development Resource
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Energy role, internal Dungeon currency, themed Dungeon energy, facility power currency
value: Dungeon Energy is the throne's primary operational and development currency. It powers construction, facilities, research, portals, training, summoning, and other System functions. Its lore name and manifestation are unique to the Dungeon Theme. Unlike material resources, it represents usable stabilized power rather than one required substance.
title: Lore — Dungeon Energy
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian Mark, Dominion currency, authenticated Mark, Lustrian trade currency
value: The Lustrian Mark is the Dominion's official currency and a common denominator among incompatible world economies. Taxes, tribute, Guilds, merchants, and the Veil use it, alongside barter. A Mark is authenticated value rather than one mandatory object and may appear as coin, note, magical seal, crystal balance, or account record.
title: Lore — Lustrian Marks
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 4 legal limit, Tier 5 authorization, Dominion charter, unsanctioned Dungeon
value: Dominion practice generally treats Tier 4 as the ceiling of unsanctioned dungeon development, not a physical limit or an identical law everywhere. A discovered dungeon seeking Tier 5+ recognition may face registration, tribute, inspection, territorial agreements, or a charter. Lower-Tier dungeons may still break law through conquest, forbidden research, illegal gates, attacks, or disputed claims.
title: Lore — Dominion Dungeon Law
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian Sector, Sector manifestation, operational Sector, Sector boundary
value: A Sector is a Lustrian region whose magical environment is internally consistent enough to map and treat as one operational area; its physical size is not fixed. Natural nexus processes, Architect systems, dungeon influence, old ruins, divine forces, magical disasters, and neighboring interference may shape its manifestation.
title: Lore — Lustrian Sectors
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Linked Servant, external Dungeon servant, bonded retainer, external bonded being
value: A Linked Servant is an existing external being joined to a dungeon bond. They are not automatically an Administrator, though one may later receive that office. Linked Servants retain an identity and origin outside the dungeon. Their access, support, obligations, and development depend on the separate Core Bond joining them to it.
title: Lore — Linked Servants
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian Rank system, operational Rank, F-to-SSS scale, ranked capability
value: Lustria uses F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, and SSS as a shared operational scale for Administrators, adventurers, threats, quests, and some professions. Rank is relative to a field, not interchangeable personal power: an A-Rank researcher and A-Rank combatant are not equivalent. Each Rank has an individual card.
title: Lore — Lustrian Rank Convention
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Wild Dungeon, instinctive Thronebound, Dungeon-created master, feral Dungeon
value: A Wild Dungeon lacks a conventional civilized Thronebound or has a master that is instinctive, incomprehensible, missing, or inseparable from the dungeon. Its origin may involve a chosen beast, dungeon-created master, failed manifestation, inherited memory, or throne operating through instinct; none is universally proven. Guilds treat Wild Dungeons as unpredictable ecological and military hazards.
title: Lore — Wild Dungeons
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: defeated Dungeon outcome, Dungeon defeat terms, postwar Dungeon, Dungeon conquest outcome
value: Dungeon defeat is not one universal result. Recognized outcomes include political Submission, metaphysical Vassalization, and Core Consumption. A victor may also receive a limited Dungeon Legacy. These concepts have separate cards because each changes sovereignty, Theme influence, resources, and possible reformation differently.
title: Lore — Dungeon Conflict Outcomes
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Realm Region Sector Site, Lustrian Region, Lustrian Site, geographic hierarchy
value: Lustria uses the practical hierarchy Realm → Region → Sector → Site. Lustria is the Realm. A Region is a broad cultural or environmental grouping. A Sector is an operational magical area. A Site is a specific city, ruin, vein, settlement, dungeon, Guild hall, fortress, anomaly, Resonance Core, or other local destination.
title: Lore — Lustrian Geographic Hierarchy
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Signature, dungeon emissions, signature fingerprint, artifact authentication
value: Every dungeon produces a metaphysical Signature derived from its throne, Theme, Thronebound, Tier, and current activity. It can authenticate portals and artifacts, distinguish populations, reveal environmental alterations, expose vassal influence, and identify emissions. Signature strength generally rises with Tier and active operations; concealment changes detection, not true identity.
title: Lore — Dungeon Signatures
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: magical Resonance, resonant compatibility, Lustrian resonance principle, resonance pattern
value: Resonance is the Lustrian principle that magical patterns influence compatible patterns. It is shared descriptive language, not proof that every phenomenon uses one mechanism. Scholars apply it to Crystals, Themes, Signatures, Anchors, bonds, Sector Cores, and vassal influence. Other cultures may explain the same relationships through divinity, biology, technology, or different magic.
title: Lore — Resonance
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: portal Anchor, recorded spatial signature, known Anchor, anchored destination
value: An Anchor is a spatial signature the dungeon has recorded and can target repeatedly. Outbound dungeon portals open only to valid known Anchors. Early Anchors normally require the Thronebound to visit the destination personally. Later methods can create transferable Gateway Anchors, but interference, suppression, or damage may still prevent a connection.
title: Lore — Portal Anchors
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Portal Gate facility, Gateway Anchor, portal throughput, stable Dungeon gate
value: A Portal Gate improves portal diameter, duration, mass throughput, traveler count, operating frequency, and destination stability. It enables durable Gateway Anchors, whose physical form adapts to the Dungeon Theme. The facility strengthens known routes; it does not eliminate Anchor requirements or external suppression.
title: Lore — Portal Gate Development
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: World Gate Array, Tier 9 gate network, coordinated major gates, interworld logistics array
value: A World Gate Array is the Tier 9 capstone of dungeon portal development. It coordinates multiple major gates, high-throughput routes, remote operations, and Homeworld–Lustria logistics while relaxing many earlier operating limits. Valid Anchors, energy, route security, and resistance from outside powers remain relevant.
title: Lore — World Gate Array
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Resonance Crystal, Crystal evolution service, evolution conduit, Resonance Crystal city
value: Resonance Crystals guide and stabilize difficult Evolution breakthroughs. Their influence enriches nearby land, so major crystals often anchor prosperous settlements, training centers, pilgrimages, and regulated or paid evolution services. A crystal assists a compatible being in crossing a threshold; it does not guarantee readiness or determine the resulting form.
title: Lore — Resonance Crystals
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: the Veil, Veil smuggler, Veil intelligence, black quest network
value: The Veil is a covert Lustrian network of traders, smugglers, mercenaries, and informants serving clients who evade Dominion oversight. It deals in restricted artifacts, intelligence, transport, and black quests. Cooperation offers discreet access and information but exposes a dungeon to betrayal, criminal rivals, and political consequences.
title: Lore — The Veil
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Verdant Accord, Lustrian independence movement, local resource movement, anti-Dungeon expansion
value: The Verdant Accord is a broad independence and stewardship movement associated with tribes, refugees, and communities seeking local control over Lustrian land and resources. It is not one uniform state or ideology. Accord-aligned groups may negotiate sustainable access, resist Dominion control, oppose dungeon extraction, or cooperate with a dungeon that respects local claims.
title: Lore — The Verdant Accord
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Administrator Capacity, major-link capacity, Administrator slot, high-order Dungeon link
value: Administrator Capacity measures how many persistent high-order links a throne can stabilize in addition to the primary Thronebound bond. Each Administrator consumes far more nexus support than an ordinary Worker or Soldier. Standard capacity is 1 + twice Dungeon Tier. Filling that capacity demonstrates stable distribution before the dungeon advances.
title: Lore — Administrator Capacity
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 0 Dungeon, newly bound Dungeon, dormant Dungeon structure
value: Tier 0 is a newly bound or reawakened dungeon. Its throne has accepted a Thronebound but supports only the Throne Room, one Administrator link, limited Gate Authority, and the minimum functions needed to become stable. The Thronebound remains Classless until Tier 1.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 0
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 1 Dungeon, first-tier Dungeon, young Dungeon foundation
value: Tier 1 is a young functional dungeon. It can establish its basic resource economy, habitation, development facilities, and first Class Selection. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 3. The dungeon has begun expressing its Theme but remains locally limited.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 1
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 2 Dungeon, second-tier Dungeon, young Dungeon expansion
value: Tier 2 is a developing young dungeon able to support Soldiers, organized training, administration, and initial Lustrian scouting. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 5. It can project power outside the Throne Room but does not yet possess mature extraction or major gates.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 2
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 3 Dungeon, third-tier Dungeon, established Dungeon entry
value: Tier 3 marks an established dungeon. It can sustain stronger defense, equipment work, population organization, and extraction from discovered Lustrian veins. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 7. External factions increasingly treat it as a durable local actor.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 3
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 4 Dungeon, fourth-tier Dungeon, established Dungeon ceiling
value: Tier 4 is a mature established dungeon with research, custom development, coordinated warfare, and major storage. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 9. Dominion practice usually treats Tier 4 as the ceiling of unsanctioned growth, though it is not a physical barrier.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 4
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 5 Dungeon, fifth-tier Dungeon, major Dungeon
value: Tier 5 is a major dungeon capable of stable interworld infrastructure and advanced education. Its Portal Gate can move people and resources more reliably, making the dungeon a geopolitical power. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 11, and discovered advancement commonly attracts Dominion authorization demands.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 5
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 6 Dungeon, sixth-tier Dungeon, major Dungeon development
value: Tier 6 is a deeply developed major dungeon able to sustain elite military cohorts and high-order construction coordination. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 13. Its infrastructure can reshape operations across multiple Sectors rather than serving only local survival.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 6
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 7 Dungeon, seventh-tier Dungeon, high-order Dungeon
value: Tier 7 is a high-order dungeon with Advanced-grade developmental potential and the ability to observe distant or dangerous Lustrian Sectors. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 15. Its Signature and environmental influence are difficult to hide through ordinary means.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 7
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 8 Dungeon, eighth-tier Dungeon, sovereign-scale Dungeon
value: Tier 8 is sovereign-scale. It can coordinate sustained conquest, govern controlled Sectors, and challenge established regional powers. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 17. Other dungeons and the Dominion judge its diplomacy, armies, and territorial ambitions as strategic threats or alliance opportunities.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 8
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 9 Dungeon, ninth-tier Dungeon, interworld Dungeon power
value: Tier 9 is an interworld power. A World Gate Array can coordinate multiple high-throughput routes, remote operations, and Homeworld–Lustria logistics. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 19. Its decisions can affect several worlds and major Lustrian political balances.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 9
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Tier 10 Dungeon, tenth-tier Dungeon, apotheotic Dungeon threshold
value: Tier 10 is the apotheotic or Architect-class threshold of known Dungeon development. It supports Mastery-grade work, perfected facilities, and sovereign capstone functions. Its standard Administrator Capacity is 21. Apotheosis grants new capabilities and deeper mysteries; it does not reveal the Architect's identity or Lustria's final purpose.
title: Lore — Dungeon Tier 10
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Administrator Level, Level 1 Administrator, Administrator experience, Administrator leveling
value: Administrator Level records experience and development accumulated after manifestation. A newly summoned Administrator normally begins at Level 1 even when their Rank is high. Levels improve through participation, quests, training, and dungeon-supported growth; they do not redefine the Administrator's original manifestation quality.
title: Lore — Administrator Level
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Administrator Rank, manifestation quality, summon Rank, Rank-up bond
value: Administrator Rank measures the quality, stability, potential, and assignment effectiveness of an Administrator's manifestation. It is distinct from Level and role. Rank is initially determined at summoning; research may improve the odds or minimum quality, while later Rank Ups require development and a sufficiently strong Thronebound bond.
title: Lore — Administrator Rank
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

value: F-Rank is the minimum stable operational classification. It indicates limited foundation or effectiveness within the measured field, not worthlessness or lack of future growth. An F-Rank Administrator can improve through experience, Bond, development, and eventual Rank Up.
title: Lore — Rank F
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

value: E-Rank indicates a limited but established operational foundation. It exceeds the minimum viable F classification while remaining below ordinary professional reliability. Rank describes present category and potential, not personality, loyalty, or Level.
title: Lore — Rank E
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

value: D-Rank indicates developing operational capability. A D-Rank individual or assignment can perform meaningful work but remains below Lustria's broadly standard C classification. Field and specialization always determine what that capability means in practice.
title: Lore — Rank D
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

value: C-Rank is the broadly standard reliable Lustrian operational classification. It represents competent function within the relevant field, not identical combat power. A C-Rank Administrator, adventurer, researcher, threat, and quest are compared within different contexts.
title: Lore — Rank C
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

value: B-Rank indicates clearly above-standard operational capability, quality, or difficulty within a field. B-Rank subjects are notable assets or hazards but remain within classifications that established Lustrian institutions can routinely plan around.
title: Lore — Rank B
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

value: A-Rank indicates exceptional operational capability, quality, or difficulty. A-Rank figures and threats command serious institutional attention. The classification remains field-specific: an A-Rank support Administrator is not automatically equivalent to an A-Rank combatant.
title: Lore — Rank A
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

value: S-Rank indicates elite capability or manifestation quality beyond ordinary professional scales. S-Rank entities are rare strategic assets or threats. A newly summoned S-Rank Administrator may still be Level 1 because Rank and accumulated experience measure different things.
title: Lore — Rank S
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

value: SS-Rank indicates extraordinary capability or quality even among elite S classifications. Institutions treat SS-Rank subjects as major strategic factors requiring specialized preparation, authority, or containment. Exact expression still depends on field, role, and specialization.
title: Lore — Rank SS
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

value: SSS-Rank is the rare upper bound of the conventional Lustrian Rank scale. It marks near-singular quality, capability, or danger within a field without declaring omnipotence. SSS remains distinct from Dungeon Tier, Evolution Tier, Grade, role, and Level.
title: Lore — Rank SSS
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon cohort, Worker cohort, Soldier cohort, cohort advancement
value: A cohort groups dungeon population by function, approximate Tier, training standard, and support level; it does not imply identical individuals. When the dungeon grows, an existing cohort does not transform at once. Qualified members gradually form a higher-Tier cohort, with training facilities increasing advancement rates. Worker Tier improves job effectiveness; Soldier Tier improves combat power.
title: Lore — Dungeon Cohorts
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Evolution Tier, personal Evolution stage, evolved Tier, biological Tier
value: Evolution Tier measures the overall stage of a being's magical and physical development: how much power they can safely contain and express. It is distinct from Dungeon Tier and Class Tier. Different bodies, species, technologies, and magical traditions can reach comparable Evolution Tiers through completely different transformations.
title: Lore — Evolution Tier
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Class, Class Selection, Class path, throne-shaped Class
value: A Dungeon Class is an organized developmental pattern shaped by the throne to direct a linked character's growth efficiently. During Class Selection, the throne presents several compatible future paths rather than dictating one destiny. Class names and manifestations follow the Dungeon Theme and individual; outside appraisers may see only Tier, Grade, and specialization.
title: Lore — Dungeon Classes
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Class Tier, Class evolution stage, Class Up, Class progression Tier
value: Class Tier records progress along one Class path. It is limited by Dungeon Tier because the throne must stabilize each higher-order pattern. A Class Up evolves the current Class, adds new Class abilities, and may branch into several compatible paths. Class Tier does not replace Level or Evolution Tier.
title: Lore — Class Tier
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Class Skill, General Skill, learned Skill, Skill mastery
value: A Skill is a learned, trained, deliberately acquired, or Class-granted capability that the user actively expresses. Skills have names, functions, mastery, and—when applicable—Grades. Combat, management, craft, movement, and supernatural techniques can all be Skills. Training improves mastery; a Skill is not an intrinsic Trait merely because it is magical.
title: Lore — Skills
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Class Trait, General Trait, intrinsic Trait, Trait mastery
value: A Trait is a persistent quality intrinsic to a being's current nature, such as resistance, physiology, perception, temperament, or a stable supernatural property. Traits may be natural, evolved, Class-granted, or purchased through dungeon development. They remain distinct from actions and techniques classified as Skills.
title: Lore — Traits
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Grade system, ability Grade, resource Grade, Grade advancement
value: Grade measures the quality, potency, structural refinement, and suitability of an ability or resource for higher-order work. It does not measure rarity alone and is distinct from Tier and Rank. Ordinary Grades progress from Grade 1 Basic through Grade 4 Mastery. Each Grade has an individual card.
title: Lore — Grades
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Grade 1, Basic Grade, Grade-1 resource, Basic-grade Skill
value: Grade 1 Basic is the first ordinary Grade. It supports foundational abilities, materials, construction, and development associated with Dungeon Tiers 1–3. Basic does not mean useless; it means the subject has not crossed the refinement threshold required for Intermediate work.
title: Lore — Grade 1 Basic
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Grade 2, Intermediate Grade, Grade-2 resource, Intermediate-grade Skill
value: Grade 2 Intermediate is the second ordinary Grade, conventionally available from Dungeon Tier 4. It represents enough purity, mastery, or structural refinement for work beyond foundational limits and normally covers Tiers 4–6.
title: Lore — Grade 2 Intermediate
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Grade 3, Advanced Grade, Grade-3 resource, Advanced-grade Skill
value: Grade 3 Advanced is the third ordinary Grade, conventionally available from Dungeon Tier 7. Advanced abilities and resources support high-order work across Tiers 7–9 and require facilities capable of producing, refining, training, or stabilizing that quality.
title: Lore — Grade 3 Advanced
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Grade 4, Mastery Grade, Grade-4 resource, Mastery-grade Skill
value: Grade 4 Mastery is the fourth ordinary Grade and corresponds to the Tier 10 threshold. It represents perfected conventional refinement rather than absolute perfection. Mastery-grade production and advancement require capstone facilities and appropriate materials.
title: Lore — Grade 4 Mastery
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: special ability Grade, nonstandard Grade, exceptional ability classification, special Grade system
value: Some abilities use special classifications outside ordinary Basic-to-Mastery progression. Unique, Apex, and Growth each describe a different reason the ordinary Grade ladder is insufficient. They are not interchangeable, and a special Grade does not automatically make an ability stronger than every ordinarily graded ability.
title: Lore — Special Ability Grades
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Unique Grade, uniquely graded ability, identity-bound ability, singular ability Grade
value: Unique Grade marks an ability defined by singular identity, origin, conditions, or expression that ordinary comparison cannot adequately describe. It may be narrow or powerful. Unique identifies exceptional individuality, not guaranteed supremacy, and its improvement follows the ability's own stated rules.
title: Lore — Unique Grade
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Apex Grade, Apex ability, peak-expression ability, apex-class Skill
value: Apex Grade marks an ability recognized as an exceptional peak expression of its kind. It is not produced by an ordinary random Grade roll and should arise from explicit lore, achievement, evolution, or singular development. Apex remains bounded by the ability's function, user, costs, and circumstances.
title: Lore — Apex Grade
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Growth Grade, Growth ability, self-evolving Skill, growth-class Trait
value: Growth Grade marks an ability whose structure can evolve beyond a fixed ordinary Grade through use, milestones, compatible resources, or defined conditions. Its current effectiveness may begin modestly. Growth describes developmental potential and rules rather than immediate superiority.
title: Lore — Growth Grade
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon detection, Dominion detection, signature tracking, Dungeon discovery chance
value: Dungeon detection is cumulative rather than purely random. Higher Tier, large portals, major construction, high-grade energy use, population activity, repeated expeditions, and territorial control strengthen observable emissions. Overseers, spies, relics, and Resonance-Core analysis can identify or investigate a Dungeon Signature.
title: Lore — Dominion Dungeon Detection
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: signature suppression, emission suppression, hidden Dungeon Tier, suppression facility
value: Signature-suppression facilities reduce detectable dungeon emissions without lowering true Dungeon Tier or changing identity. A Tier 6 dungeon might attempt to resemble Tier 4, but activity still creates evidence. Skilled Overseers, spies, relics, nearby Resonance Cores, or direct investigation may penetrate concealment.
title: Lore — Dungeon Signature Suppression
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Resonance Core, Sector Core, dormant Dungeon seed theory, local magical nexus
value: A Resonance Core is the physical or metaphysical nexus that stabilizes a Sector's local magical conditions. The Dominion monitors and claims important cores in the name of ecological stability and preventing uncontrolled dungeon emergence. Theories that cores are dormant dungeon seeds, failed thrones, immature thrones, or throne substrate remain unproven.
title: Lore — Resonance Cores
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Core Bond, bond energy allocation, Linked Servant bond, bond authority
value: A Core Bond joins an external being to a dungeon. Its support depends on compatibility, bond strength, allocated Energy, dungeon capacity, and the Thronebound's relative authority. Bonds may be voluntary, contractual, or coercive. Light bonds grant limited access and support; major bonds enable growth. Control may fail if the linked being greatly exceeds the bond's stabilizing power.
title: Lore — Core Bonds
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: quest Rank, ranked Guild quest, required adventurer Rank, mission Rank
value: Quest Rank states the operational capability considered necessary to attempt a Guild mission. It follows the F–SSS convention but does not guarantee success or prescribe the method used. A quest may be raised or lowered after new intelligence changes its danger, complexity, political sensitivity, or logistical demands.
title: Lore — Quest Rank
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: quest Category, Guild mission taxonomy, mission work type, category classification
value: Quest Category describes the kind of work a Guild mission requires rather than its difficulty. Category and Rank are assessed separately, so the same form of mission may appear anywhere on the F–SSS scale. Each standard Category has an individual card describing its purpose.
title: Lore — Quest Categories
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Survey quest, Survey mission, assessment quest
value: A Survey quest evaluates a place, route, population, resource, dungeon, or anomaly and returns reliable observations. Success depends on the requested coverage and evidence rather than defeating every threat. Survey work often establishes the information needed to assign later mission Ranks.
title: Lore — Survey Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Gathering quest, Gathering mission, collection contract
value: A Gathering quest requires collecting a specified quantity and quality of material, specimen, or product. The target may be harvested, purchased, salvaged, or otherwise acquired unless the contract limits methods. Ownership, contamination, transport, and proof of origin can affect completion.
title: Lore — Gathering Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Escort quest, Escort mission, protected travel contract
value: An Escort quest protects a person, group, caravan, creature, or shipment during travel or a dangerous operation. Completion depends on delivering the protected target under the agreed conditions. Route choice, logistics, negotiation, and avoidance may matter more than combat.
title: Lore — Escort Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Hunt quest, Hunt mission, creature hunt contract
value: A Hunt quest locates and deals with one or more creatures identified by species, behavior, territory, or threat. The contract specifies whether tracking, capture, deterrence, harvesting, or killing is required. A Hunt differs from a Bounty because its target need not be one uniquely named entity.
title: Lore — Hunt Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Investigation quest, Investigation mission, mystery contract
value: An Investigation quest determines causes, identities, motives, or hidden relationships behind an incident. Evidence quality and sound conclusions define success. Combat may occur, but destroying a suspect without resolving the requested question can fail the contract.
title: Lore — Investigation Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Defense quest, Defense mission, protection contract
value: A Defense quest protects a fixed place, population, event, resource, or operation against an expected threat. Preparations, fortification, deterrence, evacuation, and negotiation may contribute. Conditions define the protected objective and how long it must remain secure.
title: Lore — Defense Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Recovery quest, Recovery mission, retrieval contract
value: A Recovery quest retrieves a specific person, object, record, body, or lost asset. The target already has an identity and expected location or history, unlike open-ended Gathering. Preservation, secrecy, rescue, and chain of custody may be as important as return itself.
title: Lore — Recovery Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Exploration quest, Exploration mission, frontier exploration
value: An Exploration quest enters insufficiently known territory to discover routes, Sites, hazards, inhabitants, or opportunities. It is broader and less bounded than Survey work. Findings become persistent lore once observed and recorded, even when the expedition cannot fully map the area.
title: Lore — Exploration Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Subjugation quest, Subjugation mission, threat suppression contract
value: A Subjugation quest neutralizes an organized or persistent threat enough to impose control, surrender, dispersal, containment, or another stated condition. It does not always require extermination. Political consequences and the treatment of defeated groups remain part of the outcome.
title: Lore — Subjugation Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Raid quest, Dungeon Raid mission, hostile Dungeon incursion
value: A Dungeon Raid quest penetrates a dungeon to achieve a stated objective such as reconnaissance, rescue, sabotage, seizure, submission, or core assault. Dungeon hazards, population, facilities, and changing internal conditions make raids complex operations. Success does not automatically destroy the dungeon.
title: Lore — Dungeon Raid Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Bounty quest category, Bounty mission, named-target contract
value: A Bounty quest pursues one specifically identified person or entity for capture, confirmed defeat, information, or another stated disposition. Verification and legal authority matter. The target's Rank helps determine difficulty, while the Bounty Category describes the named-target structure.
title: Lore — Bounty Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Emergency quest, Emergency mission, crisis-response contract
value: An Emergency quest responds to an active crisis whose delay would sharply worsen harm. Information may be incomplete and ordinary preparation time unavailable. Guilds can revise Rank, reward, or objectives as conditions become known, while responders must balance urgency against uncontrolled escalation.
title: Lore — Emergency Quests
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Lustrian Bounty, Bounty target, Apex creature bounty, Thronebound bounty
value: A Bounty targets a specific person or entity rather than a general task. Common targets include Apex creatures, wanted criminals, rogue adventurers, dangerous magical beings, and rogue Administrators. Bounties against a Thronebound are rare, politically significant, and often connected to Dominion law, faction conflict, or dungeon warfare.
title: Lore — Lustrian Bounties
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Submission, political submission, defeated Dungeon treaty, submission terms
value: Submission is a political outcome in which a defeated dungeon accepts negotiated or imposed terms without a metaphysical dungeon-to-dungeon bond. It may owe reparations, territory, access, restrictions, or temporary tribute while retaining independent advancement, Theme, Thronebound, and Signature.
title: Lore — Dungeon Submission
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Vassalization, vassal Dungeon, overlord Dungeon, vassal core bond
value: Vassalization creates a formal dungeon-to-dungeon bond. The vassal retains its Thronebound and much of its Theme but pays tribute, accepts imposed advancement limits, and carries some influence from the overlord's Signature. Vassalage is metaphysical and strategic, not merely a treaty.
title: Lore — Dungeon Vassalization
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Core Consumption, consumed Dungeon core, Dungeon essence absorption, destroyed manifestation
value: Core Consumption destroys a defeated dungeon's current manifestation and transfers accumulated essence to the victor. It does not grant the entire foreign Theme or every ability. The underlying throne principle may eventually reform elsewhere, but whether consumption delays, alters, or can prevent that process remains unresolved.
title: Lore — Core Consumption
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon Legacy, inherited Dungeon capability, consumed core Legacy, compatible inheritance
value: A Dungeon Legacy is one limited, compatible inheritance derived from a defeated or consumed dungeon. It may influence a facility, resource, Skill, Trait, population, or other function without replacing the victor's Theme. A Legacy must be adapted through the receiving throne's own Signature and development.
title: Lore — Dungeon Legacies
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: Dungeon reformation, reformed Dungeon, dormant throne return, post-defeat rebuilding
value: A defeated dungeon may become dormant, rebuild, reconnect to another world, and seek a new Thronebound. Reformation preserves the setting's enduring dungeon principle without guaranteeing identical identity or timing. The effect of Vassalization, Core Consumption, and Legacy transfer on reformation remains a major unresolved question.
title: Lore — Dungeon Reformation
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.

keys: persistent discovery, observed canon, generated location persistence, discovered Site
value: Most Regions, Sectors, Sites, factions, and local resources receive no permanent identity until they become relevant to play. Once a place or group is observed, recorded, or meaningfully encountered, its generated identity becomes canon for that adventure. Procedural generation creates undiscovered content; it does not rewrite established discoveries.
title: Lore — Persistent Discovery
description: Setting-wide Lustria foundation shared by every dungeon; scenario-specific worlds, characters, and named dungeons are excluded.
